record.field: Discover what you can do and inspect model schemas, so every later call uses field names that actually exist.
Search, count, resolve names and aggregate any model the connection is scoped to — the foundation for questions, reports and dashboards.

List the capabilities and tools available to this connection. This connection can read Odoo data and cannot change anything; if you are asked to create or update a record, say so rather than attempting it.
List the Odoo models this connection may access and which operations (read, create, write, delete) are permitted on each.
Return the fields of a model (label, type, help, relation) so you can build correct domains and value dictionaries. Blacklisted fields are omitted.

Search a model with an Odoo domain and read fields back. The domain is a list-of-tuples given as a string. Results respect the user permissions and the scope row cap. The reply carries count, limit and has_more: when has_more is true there are further matching records beyond this page — page with offset, narrow the domain, or aggregate with read_group instead, and never present a capped page as the complete answer.

Count records matching an Odoo domain, without reading them. Cheap and safe for large models.

Resolve a text query to record ids and display names — the reliable way to turn a customer or product name into an id before searching or writing. When has_more is true the match list was truncated, so confirm with the user rather than assuming the first hit is the one they meant.

Aggregate a model by one or more fields and compute measures (sum, avg, count). This powers reports and dashboards, e.g. revenue by month or open leads by salesperson. Date fields accept a granularity suffix like create_date:month. The reply carries count, limit and has_more: when has_more is true some groups were cut off, so the totals shown are not the whole picture.
